subject: imputation using package missMDA-> factors becoming "NA". Can't figure why.

messages.author: a68f97da62f65d07
messages.subject: imputation using package missMDA-> factors becoming "NA". Can't figure why.
parts:
Hi guys,

I can't seem to figure out why my factors are becoming "NA" in red after imputation using missMDA or imputeFAMD and then checking with "complete0bs".

I start with a data set called "DA" attached in the file. as you can see, my first three columns judge, wine, and rep are factors <fct>.

If i then type in the following commands to impute missing values,
> library(missMDA)
> da.imp=imputeFAMD(DA,ncp=2)

And then i want to check if things were right, I typed in
> head(da.imp$completeObs)
I then get an outcome, which is the second picture i have attached, where the judge, wine, and rep values are all showing NA even though the missing cells from earlier do have values now, which is good, i guess. But I don't know why my judge, wine, and rep values are showing NA.

Please advise on what to do, 
i tried doing 
>  da.imp=imputeFAMD(DA,id.vars=c(4:30),ncp=2) to try to only impute from columns 4-30 (which would exclude my factor columns) but i end up getting the same result.

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: imputation using package missMDA-> factors becoming "NA". Can't figure why.
parts:
Hi

Yes, providing a reproducible example would help us to help you. It seems the problem comes from the fact that your input data is in a tibble format... strange, but at least that what happens in the example below. So simple solution would be just to use as.data.frame():
da.imp=imputeFAMD(as.data.frame(DA),ncp=2)

## Example using dataset diamonds:
library(missMDA)
library(tidyverse)

data(diamonds)
diamonds[c(3, 5), c(2,3)] <-  NA

head(imputeFAMD(head(diamonds, 1000), ncp=3)$completeObs)
head(imputeFAMD(as.data.frame(head(diamonds, 1000)), ncp=3)$completeObs)

# first one gives all vector of NA, seoncd one not...

Does this help

Matthieu
